name: Slack
tagline: Create a Slack app, make it installable in any workspace, and plug it into Composio. No review unless you list it in the Marketplace.

cost.asStated: Free. Slack doesn't charge for Marketplace listing either.

steps.title: Set up your Composio account
steps.when: Skip if you already have a Composio project and API key.
instructions: Sign up from the Composio login page.
Open Settings → API keys and copy a key.
Save it as COMPOSIO_API_KEY where your agent runs.
Stay in this project. Auth configs belong to one project.

problems.q: I can't find the API keys page
a: Open the API keys link above after signing in. It opens Settings → API keys for your current project.
If you have several projects, switch to the one you'll use for this agent first.

steps.title: Create the Slack app from a manifest
instructions: Click Create from manifest and sign in to Slack.
Pick a development workspace. You can let other workspaces install it later.
Replace "Your App Name" in the JSON (max 35 characters). Users see it on the consent screen.
Click Next, check the summary, then click Create.
Prefer the form? Create an app → Blank app, then add the values below under OAuth & Permissions.
No review. The app exists as soon as you click Create.

fields.label: App name
fields.hint: Shown to users when they connect

fields.label: Redirect URL
fields.hint: Already in the manifest. Must match your Composio auth config.

fields.label: User Token Scopes
fields.value: channels:read, channels:history, groups:read, groups:history, im:read, im:history, mpim:read, mpim:history, chat:write, users:read, reactions:write, search:read
fields.hint: Our starter set. Trim to the tools your agent uses.

warnings.text: Composio's Slack toolkit acts as the signed-in user, so the starter scopes are user scopes, not bot scopes.
warnings.unconfirmed: Composio doesn't publish its Slack scope list. This starter set is ours.

warnings.text: search:read is a legacy scope. Slack recommends Real-time Search API scopes instead.

steps.unconfirmed: The link loads, but Slack only shows the prefilled manifest after sign-in. We couldn't check that part without a Slack login.

a: display_information.name is required and can be at most 35 characters.
Each scope must be a real Slack scope name. Check spelling against Slack's scopes reference.

steps.title: Check OAuth & Permissions
instructions: In your app's settings, open OAuth & Permissions.
Under Redirect URLs, confirm the Composio callback is listed and saved.
Under Scopes → User Token Scopes, confirm your scopes.
Add Bot Token Scopes only if your Composio auth config asks for bot scopes.
Leave token rotation off unless you've confirmed Composio refreshes Slack tokens.
Leave PKCE off. It's for public clients that can't keep a secret.

warnings.text: Token rotation makes tokens expire every 12 hours, and you can't turn it off once it's on.
warnings.unconfirmed: We didn't test whether Composio refreshes rotating Slack tokens.

warnings.text: Turning on PKCE marks the app as a public client. Only Slack support can undo it.

problems.q: Slack says bad_redirect_uri when a user connects
a: The redirect URI Composio sends doesn't match a Redirect URL saved in your Slack app.
Copy the Redirect URI from your Composio auth config and add it under OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs.
A requested scope doesn't exist, or scopes conflict.
Sign in with Slack scopes (openid, profile, email) can't be mixed with other user scopes. Remove them.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret
instructions: Open Basic Information → App Credentials.
Copy the Client ID. Reveal and copy the Client Secret.
Store the secret in a secret manager, never in git.
You need the Signing Secret only for event triggers (optional step below).
Slack checks these only when a real user connects. We can't validate them for you ahead of time.

a: The Client Secret in your Composio auth config is wrong.
Copy it again from Basic Information → App Credentials and paste it with no extra spaces.
The Client ID in Composio isn't this app's.
Copy Client ID from App Credentials, not another ID on the page or the secret.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.when: Skip if only your app's own workspace will ever connect.
instructions: Open Manage Distribution → Share Your App with Other Workspaces.
Complete every item in the checklist. Redirect URLs must use HTTPS.
Click Activate Public Distribution. Slack doesn't review this.
Any workspace can now install your app. It's "unlisted": not in the Slack Marketplace.
Don't deactivate it later. That removes the app from every other workspace.

warnings.text: Since May 29, 2025, new installs of unlisted apps get 1 request/min and max 15 messages on conversations.history and .replies.
Slack's conversations.history reference still says Tier 3 and limit up to 999. The 2025 notice overrides it for unlisted apps.
Slack's API terms call the Marketplace the only appropriate channel for commercially distributed apps.

steps.unconfirmed: Slack's docs don't list the checklist items, and we couldn't open it without signing in.

a: The user is in a different workspace and your app isn't distributed yet.
Activate public distribution, then have them connect again.

problems.q: Channel history returns only 15 messages or hits rate limits
a: That's Slack's limit for new installs of unlisted apps: 1 request per minute, 15 messages per call.
Read less history, use events or search, or list the app in the Slack Marketplace.
Internal apps used only in your own org keep the higher limits.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the Slack toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Use the values below, then paste your Client ID and Client Secret.
Every scope in the auth config must also be in your Slack app, or users hit scope errors.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Must match the Slack Redirect URL exactly

fields.label: Scopes
fields.hint: Same list as your Slack app's User Token Scopes

warnings.text: Slack (acts as a user) and Slackbot (acts as a bot) are separate Composio toolkits. Each needs its own auth config.

steps.unconfirmed: Composio doesn't say whether it requests these as Slack user or bot scopes, and we couldn't open auth config creation without logging in.

problems.q: Users get missing-scope or Insufficient scopes errors
a: A scope in your auth config isn't added in the Slack app. Add it under OAuth & Permissions.
Existing tokens keep their old scopes. Users must reconnect to get new ones.

problems.q: The link didn't open the Slack toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick Slack, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for slack.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test workspace
instructions: Start a connection for a test user and open the link.
Pick a workspace. The consent screen should show your app name, not Composio.
A note that the app isn't approved by Slack is normal for unlisted apps.
Try a second workspace too, to confirm distribution works.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.
steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. It needs a Composio API key and a real Slack sign-in.

problems.q: The consent screen still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.

problems.q: Slack says the app isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace
a: That workspace only allows Marketplace apps.
An owner can turn off Only allow apps from the Slack Marketplace. See the admin approval step below.

problems.q: Slack asks the user to submit a request
a: The workspace has Require approved apps on. An owner or admin must approve the install.
Owners can install directly. Members need approval.

steps.title: Get workspace admin approval
steps.when: Only if a user's workspace requires approved apps or Marketplace-only apps.
instructions: Your user requests the app on Slack's install screen.
A workspace owner or app manager approves the request.
Or an owner turns off Require approved apps and Only allow apps from the Slack Marketplace.
Those live in Admin → Apps and workflows → App management settings.
Admins see your full scope list. Fewer scopes make approval easier.
steps.unconfirmed: Slack's docs don't say how long a pending request lasts or whether the user is notified when it's approved.

problems.q: The admin won't allow non-Marketplace apps
a: Only a Slack Marketplace listing gets past a Marketplace-only policy.
See the optional Marketplace steps below.

steps.title: Send Slack events to Composio triggers
steps.when: Only if your agent uses Composio Slack triggers.
instructions: Copy the Signing Secret from Basic Information → App Credentials.
For DMs, private channels or reactions, create an App-Level Token with authorizations:read.
Create a Composio webhook endpoint for slack with both values.
Paste its webhook_url into Event Subscriptions → Request URL. Composio answers Slack's check.

warnings.text: Store the secret in Composio before setting the Request URL. Slack may disable an endpoint after ~36 hours of failures.

problems.q: Slack events never reach my trigger
a: Check the endpoint has the Signing Secret. Unsigned or mismatched requests get a 400.
For DMs, private channels and reactions, add the App-Level Token too.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.when: Optional. Lifts the unlisted rate limits and works in Marketplace-only workspaces.
instructions: First reach 10+ installs on active workspaces (used in the past 28 days). Stay at 10+ during review.
Test install, onboarding, use and uninstall on a workspace other than your dev one.
Open Submit to the Slack Marketplace in your app settings. Fix what the automated checks flag.
Give Slack test account credentials and a short demo video from install to uninstall.
Request only the scopes your features need. Slack reviews each one.

warnings.text: Slack cut the bar to 5 active workspaces in August 2025, then raised it back to 10 in July 2026.
Not accepted: apps that only provide an MCP server, or that use Slack data to train LLMs.
Automation platforms must limit installs to paid Slack plans, using the team.billing:read bot scope.

a: Slack blocks submissions under 10 installs on active workspaces.
Active means used in the past 28 days. Sandboxes don't count.
Slack returns apps that aren't production-ready or that it can't install.
Fix every point and resubmit. In preliminary review, each resubmission resets your queue spot.

steps.title: Wait for Marketplace review
steps.when: Only after you submit to the Slack Marketplace.
instructions: Preliminary review: feedback in up to 10 business days.
Functional review: up to 10 weeks for new apps, 6 weeks for changes to published apps.
Feedback arrives in your app settings and by email. Address every point.
Slack can't speed it up. Once approved, you choose when to publish.

wait.asStated: Up to 10 business days for preliminary feedback, then up to 10 weeks for functional review.

problems.q: Review is taking longer than stated
a: Slack says times vary with volume. Check the estimate on your app's submission page.
For process questions, email the Marketplace team.
